explain: Logs describe events, traces relate operations, metrics aggregate trends, and audit/evaluation records serve separate purposes. One signal cannot replace all the others.
steps: Build a minimal artifact for each operational signal. || Inspect their distinct structures without exporting private data.
name: signals

explain: A function can execute successfully while the business task returns not_found. Separate those categories in telemetry and alerts.
steps: Record transport execution separately from domain outcome. || Count the business failure without inventing an exception.
name: outcome-not-exception

explain: Metric labels should use bounded categories rather than per-user or per-task values. High-cardinality IDs belong only in appropriately controlled diagnostic records.
steps: Select low-cardinality labels from the event. || Exclude task and user identity from the aggregate metric dimensions.
name: metric-cardinality

explain: Missing usage or pricing is unknown, not zero spend. Preserve that state so billing and operational reconciliation can distinguish it.
steps: Check usage and price availability before multiplication. || Leave cost unset when the inputs are unavailable.
name: cost-unknown

explain: An alert corresponds to user impact and points to a runbook. Queue age can reveal stalled work even when process liveness remains green.
steps: Compare the oldest task age with the declared budget. || Emit a bounded alert name and response reference rather than a raw payload dump.
name: impact-alert
